title: The load event is LoadCompleted (EV-26) in the build notes and AceDataReady (EV-26) in the architecture catalogue
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-001 step 1, RWB-E2-007 step 1, RWB-E2-008 step 1, RWB-E2-034 step 1; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx, Events sheet row EV-26; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md, slide 43 (event catalogue 2/2, row 26)
section: How to read this version; RWB-E2-001, RWB-E2-007, RWB-E2-008, RWB-E2-034
description: The four stories name the load event LoadCompleted (EV-26) and say JOB-01 publishes it. The Arch v5 catalogue names EV-26 AceDataReady with rwb-source-data as producer. This version uses the catalogue name and producer, so the event a consumer subscribes to in the target reads AceDataReady, while the legacy name LoadCompleted stays in the Epic 1 material.
evidence: Build notes steps read "JOB-01 publishes LoadCompleted (EV-26)"; Ownership Map Events row EV-26 basis reads "slide 43 row 26 ... rwb-source-data as producer of AceDataReady"; Architecture v5 slide 43 names EV-26 AceDataReady.
owner_role: Solution architect with the integration lead
proposed: Keep AceDataReady (EV-26) as the target event name on rwb.source-data.events.v1 and list LoadCompleted as its legacy alias in the Event and Messaging next version and the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog v1.

title: JOB-01 is retired, yet three Epic 2 stories are keyed on it
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-001 step 1, RWB-E2-010 step 1, RWB-E2-034 step 4; Ownership Map v1.xlsx, Jobs sheet row JOB-01
description: The stories start the hand-over, the stage 2 product step and the EFS contact import on JOB-01. The Jobs sheet retires JOB-01 under D-RCV-35 and replaces it with ACE ingestion read through the rwb-source-data view contract, so this version starts them on AceDataReady (EV-26) and the rwb-source-data ingest workflow AceIngestCheck (JOB-04).
evidence: Jobs sheet JOB-01 replacement reads "none (retired under D-RCV-35; ACE ingestion, read through the rwb-source-data ACE view contract)"; the three build notes steps name JOB-01 as their trigger.
owner_role: Integration lead with the solution architect
proposed: Confirm in the Batch and Scheduling next version that no Epic 2 step depends on JOB-01, and carry AceIngestCheck (JOB-04) and AceDataReady (EV-26) as the only entry points.

title: JOB-05 and TimerDue (EV-18) are retired, yet three Epic 2 stories are keyed on them
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-004 step 7, RWB-E2-015 step 5, RWB-E2-035 step 7; Ownership Map v1.xlsx, Jobs sheet row JOB-05 and Events sheet row EV-18
description: Three stories read or change the JOB-05 five-minute timer check and one polls it for cases with no next action. The Jobs sheet retires JOB-05 in favour of durable timers inside each workflow, and the Events sheet marks TimerDue (EV-18) retired. This version replaces the check with durable Temporal timers and, for the next-action scan, with a five-minute Temporal Schedule in rwb-case.
evidence: Jobs sheet JOB-05 replacement reads "no Temporal Schedule (durable timers inside each workflow; the 5-minute timer check is retired)"; Events row EV-18 ruling reads "TimerDue is not a rwb-case event type".
owner_role: Solution architect with the case and workflow lead
proposed: Register the five-minute next-action Schedule in the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1 and delete EV-18 from the Epic 2 contract tables.

title: RWB-E2-009 writes an INT-19 extract for a data lake that the target removes
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-009 steps 4 and 5; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 row DP-17
description: The steering dashboard story publishes a day only when it has written the INT-19 extract to the data lake, and the Power BI data set refreshes from that extract. The target removes the data lake and INT-19 (DP-17), so the story needs lake data that no longer exists. This version replaces the extract with published measure rows and measure events on rwb.reporting.events.v1 that the data set reads from rwb-reporting.
evidence: Build notes RWB-E2-009 step 4 reads "write the INT-19 extract for the data lake with its freshness stamp"; DP-17 reads "Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 - removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting".
owner_role: Reporting and BI lead with the data product owner
proposed: Name the read model or event topic the Power BI data set subscribes to after the data lake removal, and update the acceptance criteria of RWB-E2-009 once.

title: RWB-E2-027 loads a payment_match_rule table that RWB-E2-042 forbids
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-027 step 1 and RWB-E2-042 risk note; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 row DP-04
description: RWB-E2-027 loads a payment_match_rule reference table through the reference load endpoint and reads it with a repository. RWB-E2-042 states that its schema check asserts no payment_match_rule table exists, and that the match rows live in the PAYMENT_MATCH rule package. This version reads the rules through RuleCatalog.row and creates no match rule table.
evidence: Build notes RWB-E2-027 step 1 reads "loads a parameter version ... with table payment_match_rule"; RWB-E2-042 risk note reads "the schema check asserts that no payment_match_rule table exists".
owner_role: Solution architect with the decision and rules lead
proposed: Drop the match rule table from every service schema and keep the PAYMENT_MATCH package as the only home of the rows, with the load through the rule package endpoints.

title: The payment match priority order differs between RWB-E2-027 and RWB-E2-042
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-027 step 4 and RWB-E2-042 step 4; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md
description: RWB-E2-027 tries the rows as EXACT, then WINDOW, then PARTIAL. RWB-E2-042 fixes the package order as EXACT, then PARTIAL, then WINDOW. The Drools design ranks above the story master, so this version uses EXACT, then PARTIAL, then WINDOW and records the change on the story.
evidence: Build notes RWB-E2-027 step 4 reads "priority order (EXACT, then WINDOW, then PARTIAL)"; RWB-E2-042 step 4 reads "The PaymentMatch package keeps EXACT, then PARTIAL, then WINDOW".
owner_role: Decision and rules lead with the payment lead
proposed: Confirm the order with Credit Administration and carry it in the PAYMENT_MATCH scenario set, so one order is tested and no run depends on two.

title: The partner_user table is created by P4 in the story and owned by S9 in the ownership map
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-019 step 3; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json item partner_user; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (S9 partner users)
description: RWB-E2-019 creates partner_user with its own migration under the P4 story. The ownership ruling gives partner users to S9 rwb-partner, and P4 keeps the internal role, scope and masking model. This version puts the table and its migration in the rwb_partner sequence and leaves the identity, role and session work with rwb-access.
evidence: Ownership ruling reads "Partner users stay with S9 rwb-partner (Architecture v5 slide 41, partner users); P4 keeps the internal role model only"; the build notes step reads "Create the table partner_user with the migration V_E2_019__partner_user.sql".
owner_role: Access lead with the partner lead
proposed: Move the DDL and the reference load handler to the S9 story set and keep the session, role and scope checks in rwb-access.

title: The signature_request table is created by P6 in the story and owned by P5 in the ownership map
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-018 step 4; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json item signature_request; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 41
description: RWB-E2-018 creates signature_request in a V2_018 migration under the P6 story. The ownership ruling gives signatures to P5 rwb-document, and P6 orchestrates the request through the P5 contract. This version puts the table and its migration in the rwb_document sequence and keeps the flow and the listeners in rwb-comms.
evidence: Ownership ruling reads "signature_request is P5 rwb-document (Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41, signatures); P6 orchestrates the request through P5's contract"; the build notes step reads "Create the table in the migration V2_018__signature_request.sql".
owner_role: Document hub lead with the communications lead
proposed: Move the signature_request DDL to the P5 story set and publish the request and result operations on the rwb-document contract.

title: JOB-09 is retired, yet RWB-E2-021 loads the INT-15 result file with it
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-021 step 6; Ownership Map v1.xlsx, Jobs sheet row JOB-09
description: The letter dispatch story loads the INT-15 delivery result file in JOB-09. The Jobs sheet retires JOB-09 under D-RCV-35 and reads the ACE result through the rwb-source-data view contract. This version has rwb-source-data read the file and publish the delivery result, which rwb-comms consumes.
evidence: Jobs sheet JOB-09 replacement reads "none (retired under D-RCV-35; ACE ingestion, read through the rwb-source-data ACE view contract)"; the build notes step reads "JOB-09: loads the INT-15 file".
owner_role: Integration lead with the communications lead
proposed: Name the delivery result event and its topic in the Event and Messaging next version, and delete the JOB-09 loader from the Epic 2 story set.

title: Quartz triggers appear in RWB-E2-037 and RWB-E2-039 after Quartz is retired
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-037 step 2 and RWB-E2-039 step 3; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 row DP-10 and section R6 row Retired
description: One story runs the stuck-workflow scanner on Quartz and the other states that the archive job is not on a Temporal Schedule. The target retires Quartz and RWB-TE-007, and DP-10 moves every job to a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow. This version runs both jobs as Temporal Schedules on rwb-platform.
evidence: Build notes RWB-E2-037 reads "runs every 15 minutes on Quartz"; RWB-E2-039 reads "not on a Temporal Schedule"; Template and Rules R6 retires RWB-TE-007 (Quartz scheduler: replaced by Temporal Schedules in RWB-PLT-E1071).
owner_role: Platform lead with the DevOps team
proposed: List both jobs as Temporal Schedules in the Temporal Workflow and Activity Catalog v1 and remove the Quartz option from the run books.

title: RWB-E2-023 has no row in the plan, so it has no service, lane or new stories
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json blocks legacy and slices; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-023
section: RWB-E2-023; Realignment map by service and lane
description: The plan holds 41 RWB-E2 keys and none of them is RWB-E2-023, and no slice carries that legacy key. The build notes do carry the story, under the P2 Integration module. This version takes its primary service from the source module line and writes the placeholder of section R9 for its new stories and lanes.
evidence: The plan legacy block holds no RWB-E2-023 row; the 42 story headings of the build notes include RWB-E2-023.
owner_role: Product owner with the integration lead
proposed: Add a slice set for RWB-E2-023 with rwb-integration as primary service, register it in the plan, and re-run the story split for wave 2.

source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md (story headings); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Catalog v1.xlsx, Stories sheet; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json
section: Realignment map by service and lane
description: The Epic 2 stories run from RWB-E2-001 to RWB-E2-043 and none of them is RWB-E2-020. The catalogue and the plan also hold no RWB-E2-020 row. Nothing states whether the story was withdrawn or never written, so this version keeps the numbering as it is and records the gap.
evidence: The 42 story headings of the build notes hold no RWB-E2-020; the catalogue Stories sheet holds no RWB-E2-020 row; the plan legacy block holds no RWB-E2-020 key.

title: RWB-E2-033 to RWB-E2-036 sit in the P2 backlog while their code and tables are in rwb-case
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-033 to RWB-E2-036 module lines and RWB-E2-036 step 1; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy block; Ownership Map v1.xlsx Tables sheet
description: Four stories are labelled P2 Integration, and RWB-E2-036 itself states that its code sits in the case and workflow folders because the queue and case tables belong to P3. The plan keeps rwb-integration as primary for all four. This version keeps the plan primary so the story set does not change, and records the tension for the assembly step.
evidence: Build notes RWB-E2-036 step 1 reads "The code sits in folder recovery/casewf/placement even though the story is in the P2 backlog, because the queue and case tables belong to P3"; the plan gives these four keys primary P2.
owner_role: Solution architect with the case and workflow lead
proposed: Decide whether the four stay in the rwb-integration backlog with P3 delta stories or move to RWB-SVC-P3, and apply the answer once in the plan.

title: The payment match rule load is a P4 reference load in the story and a P7 rule package in the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Build Notes Epic 2 v3.md, RWB-E2-027 step 1; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx, Services and Tables sheets; Template and Rules v1 section R3 default rulings
description: The story posts the match rule file to the reference load endpoint owned by P4 and applies it with a handler in the P8 module. The default ruling puts the rule package registry in P7 rwb-decision, and the load of a package runs through the rwb-decision endpoints. This version keeps the reference data administrator as the loader and moves the load itself to rwb-decision.
evidence: Build notes RWB-E2-027 step 1 reads "P4 owns the endpoint. Your work is PaymentMatchRuleLoadHandler"; Template and Rules R3 default ruling reads "Rule package registry | P7 rwb-decision".
owner_role: Decision and rules lead with the access lead
proposed: Keep one load path for rule packages in rwb-decision, and use the P4 reference load endpoint only for reference data that is not a rule package.
